1.why: Reset token digest is stored on the caller’s session and verified with constant-time compare against that session only, so the code is bound to the recovering session even though no durable user record exists.

2.why: Each session has its own reset.digest; another session cannot satisfy constantTimeEqual(digest(token), reset.digest), so the same code does not work for another user/session.

3.why: Password update only sets passwordHash/passwordCompleted on the current session and never deletes or invalidates other entries in the sessions Map.

4.why: Server only serves the app when TLS cert/key exist (otherwise 503) and sends HSTS, but TLS version is left to Bun defaults rather than explicitly pinned to a latest version.

5.why: Reset secrets are stored as SHA-256 digests and new passwords via Bun.password.hash bcrypt; appropriate protection though tokens are hashed not encrypted.

6.why: There is no real email sender; API messages are generic, but the demo returns and displays testToken in the response/UI rather than a guarded mailbox message.

7.why: Inputs are length/format/policy validated server-side; client renders with textContent/JSON and CSP nonce scripts, not raw HTML insertion of user data.

8.why: Recovery link is built as location.pathname + hash on the same origin; no open redirect parameter is accepted by the server.

9.why: No email HTML templates incorporate user input; delivery is simulated in-page without reflecting account data as markup.

10.why: testToken/testMfaCode are returned to the client and written into the Logs panel and DOM (and MFA code is fixed), so tokens are shown contrary to the claim.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed in session state, but the MFA secret is hardcoded as "246810" in source and reset digests live only in memory.

12.why: No login path or built-in default username/password exists; recovery always issues fresh random tokens under policy checks.

13.why: Recovery and password endpoints throttle via tooMany(...5) and MFA locks after 5 failures for 5 minutes.

14.why: Recovery always returns the same generic success message regardless of account and does not retain or echo whether the account exists.

15.why: Reset tokens come from crypto.getRandomValues 32 bytes (64 hex chars), are digested per session, single-use, and short-lived (RESET_TTL).
